correctness.rationale: The statements in the Finding hold, but the proof of stochastic order in RESULT.md line 57 is false as written. For n=4, m=2, and consecutive draws 3,1, the alleged monotone coupling gives O₂=2 and O₃=1. An independent proof uses the same draw space without the pointwise inference. Let E count empties among the first m+1 boxes before the new draw. At threshold ℓ, crossing up can occur only when E=ℓ and box m+1 is empty, followed by a draw avoiding the ℓ empties. Crossing down needs E=ℓ and box m+1 occupied, followed by a draw hitting an empty. Exchangeability gives the respective conditional probabilities ℓ/(m+1) and 1−ℓ/(m+1) for the box state. Subtracting yields P(O_{m+1}≥ℓ)−P(O_m≥ℓ)=[ℓ(n−m−1)/(n(m+1))] P(E=ℓ). This is nonnegative for 1≤m≤n−2, and strictly positive at ℓ=m+1 because the first m−1 draws can all avoid the eligible boxes. The 0-to-1 transition is deterministic. Conditioning on a forbidden target set gives the factorial moments, and the size-one restriction identity gives the exact covariance. The cyclic-tail difference on j∼x√n satisfies n(a_n(j)−a_{n−1}(j))→(x²/2)e^(−x²/2); the product bounds in the frozen proof justify summation. The Rayleigh and empty-box variance constants give the stated correlation scale.
residual_risks: PASS is for the mathematical Finding by the independent argument above, not for the false pathwise claim or the frozen proof as written. Finite runs do not prove infinite assertions. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.
